text:
Sam O'Reilly's NHL career is three games old. The Lightning recalled him from AHL Syracuse, and on Nov. 11 in Buffalo he took his rookie lap, then picked up an assist in his debut, an 8-3 win. The Canadian Hockey League's headline called him a "Two-time Memorial Cup champion," and he arrives with a résumé of winning in junior.

Tampa Bay got him from Edmonton in July 2025 for Isaac Howard, a year after the Oilers took him 32nd overall. His last junior season produced 71 points in 56 OHL games, and he had 8 points in 7 games for Canada at the 2026 World Juniors.

Three games is far too few to judge anything, and our numbers treat it that way. He has played about 13 minutes a night with 1 point, 7 hits and 2 shots. His talent range is wide, which is what an empty NHL record looks like. For context, of the forwards picked 27th to 37th since 2005 who lasted four-plus seasons, 40 of 103 reached 200 NHL games. What to watch is simple: whether his minutes hold, and whether he stays up.
headline: O'Reilly gets his first NHL look in Tampa
